items.note: Three studies in which people rate the helpfulness and harm of LLM-generated cross-domain analogies for problem reformulation; the abstract names no condition without AI or with another AI configuration, so check the full text for a comparison condition.

Undergraduate design course comparing an AI-assisted teaching path (DeepSeek LLM) with a traditional path on design quality (72.43 vs 65.60), with cognitive-load SEM; assignment and sample size not stated in the abstract.

Controlled comparison of manual, human-AI collaborative, and full-AI print-ad design modes over 80 tasks (240 design samples) scored on quality, brand fit, and creative depth, with 300 audience survey respondents as raters; the number of designers is not stated and the design may be closer to AI-versus-human output.

User study with 24 novice designers comparing ConceptVis (LLM plus interactive knowledge graph) with a chat-based LLM interface on concept generation, reporting less repetitive concepts and better ideation performance; an earlier IDETC 2024 version exists.

Between-subjects experiment (N=247) on two-round plastic-pollution ideation varying timing (early vs late) and labeling of AI suggestions against a no-AI control, with rated creativity and divergence outcomes; a duplicate Crossref record 10.24963/ijcai.2024/1142 exists.

Within-subjects study (N=16 teachers) comparing the LitLinker LLM system with an LLM chatbot for ideating interdisciplinary teaching contexts, measuring integration depth of ideas and workload; condition order not stated.

Controlled experiment with 36 participants in pairs using a digital collaboration tool with or without AI features, scoring idea novelty and appropriateness (AI pairs more novel, less appropriate, not significant).

Counterbalanced brainstorming experiment comparing human-only, human-agent (multi-agent LLM framework), and agent-only conditions on general and domain-specific topics, with originality scores and BERT-embedding semantic dispersion; participant count not stated.

Wizard-of-Oz study with 20 mechanical designers using generative design tools with or without metacognitive support agents, finding agent-supported users made more feasible designs; compares AI configurations, exploratory.

Seven students generated ideas individually or in groups with AI tools, with creativity examined from participant views and outputs; the abstract does not state a no-AI comparison, so the contrast may be individual vs group only.
